nodes.title: PAT-ChIP
nodes.scope: Illumina PAT-ChIP explanatory schematic: one linear route from FFPE-fixed pathology chromatin through deparaffination/rehydration, MNase digestion, sonication, immunoprecipitation/elution, crosslink reversal/proteinase K digestion and purification to DNA. The separate far-left PAT-ChIP title illustration is descriptive, not an additional operation or branch. The diagram has no library-preparation or sequencing block, no legend assigning chemical identities to colors, and no specified DNA end groups. The card mentions FiT-seq as a distinct refinement, but the supplied abstract does not resolve its operation-by-operation relationship to this route. Downstream library/readout interpretation is limited to DNA recovered by chromatin-target enrichment.

original.label: FFPE-fixed chromatin
features: Chromatin from formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded pathology tissue; DNA remains associated with chromatin proteins.
The yellow nucleosome drawing at far left captions the assay and is not connected as a separate input or branch.

evidence.locator: Main workflow, left: nucleosome array labeled "FFPE-fixed chromatin"; the separate far-left yellow nucleosome illustration is captioned "Pathology tissue chromatin immunoprecipitation (PAT-ChIP)".
Abstract (supplied abstract only): method definition
evidence.quote: Here we describe pathology tissue chromatin immunoprecipitation (PAT-ChIP), a technique for extraction and high-throughput analysis, by techniques such as ChIP-seq, of chromatin derived from FFPE samples.

original.label: Deparaffinated, rehydrated chromatin
features: Intermediate boundary between removal of paraffin/rehydration and MNase digestion; no separate isolated intermediate is drawn.

evidence.locator: Main workflow, arrow labeled "Deparaffination and rehydration", between "FFPE-fixed chromatin" and the chromatin illustration labeled "MNase digestion".
evidence.rationale: The named deparaffination/rehydration arrow precedes the MNase-labeled chromatin; this boundary separates the two depicted operations.

evidence.locator: Description / jcr:content/par/text_1/text
evidence.quote: PAT-ChIP is a variation of ChIP-Seq, optimized for the analysis of chromatin derived from FFPE samples. The distinguishing features of this method are dewaxing with a xylene substitute (Histolemon, Carlo Erba) followed by both MNase digestion and sonication. FiT-seq introduces further refinements to this method.

original.label: MNase-digested chromatin
features: Chromatin has undergone nuclease digestion and is still depicted as DNA associated with nucleosomal particles.
Orange circles accompany the MNase digestion label; no legend specifies their chemistry, and no DNA end groups are drawn.

evidence.locator: Main workflow, "MNase digestion": orange circles appear around nucleosomal chromatin; the rightward arrow leads to a shorter chromatin illustration before "Sonicate".

original.label: Soluble extract
features: Soluble chromatin fragments after sonication, depicted as nucleosomal particles with attached DNA.

evidence.locator: Main workflow, arrow labeled "Sonicate", from the chromatin illustration after "MNase digestion" to the nucleosomal fragments labeled "Soluble extract".

original.label: Immunoprecipitated and eluted chromatin
features: Selected chromatin retains DNA associated with chromatin protein before crosslink reversal.

evidence.locator: Main workflow, "Soluble extract" and pink antibody-like capture illustration; rightward arrow labeled "Immunoprecipitate and chromatin elution" leads to a single nucleosome-like particle.

original.label: DNA after crosslink reversal and proteinase K digestion
features: DNA is depicted as a blue line after the protein-associated particle; it is no longer shown wrapped around a nucleosome.
No strand count, end polarity, or chemical modification is specified by the line icon.

evidence.locator: Main workflow, isolated nucleosome-like particle and pink/green enzyme-like icon above the arrow labeled "Reverse crosslink and proteinase K digestion"; output is a blue line.

original.label: Purified DNA
features: Terminal product explicitly labeled DNA; derives from the immunoprecipitated chromatin fraction.

Downstream ChIP-seq uses the recovered DNA sequence to locate genomic regions associated with the selected histone modification or transcription factor. This is a library interface interpretation; library construction and sequencing are not depicted.

A sequencing library would represent the recovered, antibody-enriched DNA fragments, not direct sequencing of histone marks or proteins. Enrichment does not establish perfect target specificity or unbiased recovery.

evidence.locator: Main workflow, right end: blue line before the arrow labeled "Purification"; terminal blue line labeled "DNA".

evidence.quote: analyses of histone modifications and transcription factor binding on a genome-wide scale using patient-derived FFPE samples.
evidence.rationale: Combined with the figure's immunoprecipitation-to-DNA route and the abstract's ChIP-seq definition, this supports interpreting recovered DNA as the genomic carrier of the selection history. No library chemistry or specificity guarantee follows.
